paragraphs: Rabbi Pappi (an Amora in the Land of Israel, in the fourth generation).

He is mentioned in Shabbat 151b: “R' Levi said: R' Pappi said: R' Yehoshua said: After three days his belly splits open and falls upon his face,” etc. Hyman calls this a mistaken reading, and reports that in Dikdukei Soferim it reads: “R-P said in the name of R' Yehoshua of Sikhnin.”
And in the Jerusalem Talmud the statement is cited: “R' Abba son of R-P, and R' Yehoshua of Sikhnin, said in the name of R' Levi.”
And in Yevamot, chapter 16, halakha 3, the statement appears, and there: “R' [Abba], his son, and Rav Pappi, R' Yehoshua of Sikhnin, in the name of R' Levi.”

Hyman says that the true reading remained in Vayikra Rabbah, beginning of chapter 18, where it reads: “Rabbi Abba bar Kahana in the name of R' Pappi, and Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnin in the name of Rabbi Levi; Rabbi Akiva expounded all three,” etc. Afterwards it cites: “Rabbi Abba son of R' Pappi and Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnin in the name of Rabbi Levi.” And it appears to Hyman that one should read: R' Abba כ״כ in the name of R-P and R-Y of Sikhnin, B-Sh-L.

And in Bava Batra 75b: “R' Levi said: Rav Pappi said in the name of R' Yehoshua of Sikhni: If there are three Jerusalems,” etc. In Dikdukei Soferim the reading is: “R' Levi said, and some say R' Pappi, in the name of R-Y of Sikhnin.”
From all these places, Hyman says, we see that he was a student of R' Yehoshua of Sikhnin, who was renowned for his aggadic teaching, the student of R' Levi.

The whole printed notice spans volume III, pp. 1030–1031. The consulted Shabbat 151b passage gives Rabbi Levi reporting Rav Pappei reporting Rabbi Yehoshua, with the belly bursting after three days; Hyman’s judgment that the reading is mistaken and his Dikdukei Soferim alternative remain his apparatus report. The whole consulted Vayikra Rabbah 18:1 has distinct chains: Rabbi Abba bar Kahana in the name of Rav Pappei; Rabbi Chiyya son of Rabbi Pappei; and Rabbi Abba son of Rav Pappei. It directly says that Rabbi Akiva expounded all three matters. The names, titles and chains are not silently merged. The relevant whole Jerusalem Talmud passage is at Yevamot 16:3 in the consulted Guggenheimer edition, beside Hyman’s supplied 15:3; the English cites the consulted location and the Hebrew remains unchanged. That passage reads Rabbi Ba in the name of Rav Pappai, followed by Rabbi Yehoshua of Sukhnin in the name of Rabbi Levi, and continues with the soul and body after three days. It does not independently establish Hyman’s supplied missing-name/son/AND Rav Pappi wording. The bracketed [Abba] in the English is an inherited editorial supply, not a name printed by Hyman, notwithstanding the older note’s description. His tentative reconstruction, literal כ״כ and final B-Sh-L remain unexpanded. Bava Batra 75b directly has Rav Pappei and the conditional alternatives of three or thirty Jerusalems; its fuller continuation is not inserted into the biography. Exact Dikdukei Soferim readings and correction history remain uncollated, and Hyman’s confident final teacher inference remains his inference. All existing notes are preserved verbatim as records of their earlier review stages.
